Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 50, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Qaf (ق), because it opens with this letter from the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) found at the beginnings of some surahs.

Some Aims of the Surah

• It mentions the position of those who denied the Message and the Resurrection, and the cause of their denial, and it argues for the proof of the Resurrection through sensory evidence, such as the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is upon them, the revival of the earth after its death by the water of the sky, and the growth of trees and fruits.

• It clarifies the comprehensiveness of God's knowledge of hidden things and the thoughts of souls, and that every person is under God's observation from birth until death.

• It reminds the disbelievers of the nations that were destroyed before them, who were stronger than them, and it alerts them to God's power to create great creations without fatigue or exhaustion, and it consoles the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding their denial of him.

[The Tafsir]

﴿Qaf﴾. The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah. God, Exalted, swears by the Noble Qur'an, the Possessor of glory and honor.

Rather, those who denied the Messenger (ﷺ) were amazed that a warner from among them had come to them, warning them of God's punishment. So the disbelievers in God and His Messenger said: "This is a strange thing, something to be astonished at."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 50, verse 3:

"When we have died and become dust, how could it be possible to return to what we were after that? That return is far-fetched and unlikely to occur."

We already know what the earth consumes and diminishes of their bodies, and with Us is a preserved Book, safeguarded from alteration and substitution, recording everything that happens to them in their lifetimes and after their deaths.
Rather, these polytheists denied the Qur'an when it came to them. So they are in a confused, muddled state of affairs: they do not hold firm to anything, and they have no settled footing.

Have they not looked at the sky above them, when they disbelieve in the Resurrection? How We built it, making it level in its extent and firm in its construction, and adorned it with stars, and it has no cracks or fissures, so it is free from disparity and defects?

And the earth — We spread it out and laid it flat, and We placed in it firm mountains, lest it sway with its inhabitants, and We caused to grow in it every kind of beautiful, beneficial plant, which delights and gladdens the one who looks upon it.

Allah created the heavens and the earth, and what is in them of great signs, as a lesson by which one gains sight from the blindness of ignorance, and a reminder for every servant who is humble, fearful and anxious, who turns back in repentance to Allah, mighty and majestic is He.
And We sent down from the sky blessed rain, abundant in benefits, and caused to grow by it gardens of many trees, and grain that is harvested.
And We caused the palm trees to grow tall, bearing clusters of blossom (ṭalʿ) layered one upon another.

We caused gardens to grow thereby as provision for the servants, which they sustain themselves with according to their needs. And by this water which We sent down from the sky We brought to life a land that had become barren and parched, with no crop or vegetation in it, just as We brought the dead land to life with that water. Thus shall We bring you forth on the Day of Resurrection, alive after death.

Before these pagan Quraysh, the people of Noah, the people of al-Rass (the well), Thamud, ʿAd, Pharaoh, the people of Lot, the people of al-Aykah (the thicket), the people of Shuʿayb, and the people of Tubbaʿ al-Ḥimyari denied their messengers. All of these nations denied their messengers, so the threat that Allah had promised them for their disbelief was fulfilled against them.

Did We tire of originating the first creation, which We brought into being when it was nothing, so that We would be unable to recreate them as a new creation after they have perished? That does not overpower Us. Rather, We are fully capable of it. But they are in confusion and doubt about the matter of resurrection and rising again.
We created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than his jugular vein, which is a vein in the neck connected to the heart.
When the two angels who keep watch, one on his right and one on his left, record his deeds. The one on the right records the good deeds, and the one on the left records the bad deeds.
No word is uttered that a person speaks, except that there is with him an angel (malak) watching his speech and recording it, and this angel is present and prepared for that task.
The intensity of death and its overwhelming pangs came with the truth that cannot be turned back or escaped. That is what you, O human, used to flee from and evade.
And the second blast is blown into the "Horn," the trumpet-blast of resurrection. That blowing will be on the day when the threat that God made to the disbelievers comes to pass.
And every soul will come, accompanied by two angels: one driving it to the place of gathering, and the other bearing witness against it for what it did in the world, of good and evil.
You were heedless of this, O man, which you now see clearly today. So We have removed from you your covering that veiled your heart, and your sight today is sharp and piercing.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 50, verse 23:

The angel who was recording (the deeds), the witness over him, will say: "This is what I have from his register of deeds; it is ready with me, preserved and present."

God says to the two angels, the driver and the witness, after He has separated the creatures: "Cast into Hell every ungrateful disbeliever, who is excessive in disbelief and in denying God, obstinate against the truth, withholding what is due of his rights in his wealth, transgressing against the servants of God and against His limits, doubtful about His promise and His threat, who associated another deity with God and worshipped alongside Him another god from among His creation. So cast him into the severe torment of Hell."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 50, verse 27:

His devil, who had been with him in the world, said: "Our Lord, I did not lead him astray, but he was on a distant path, far from the way of guidance."

God Almighty says: "Do not dispute before Me today, in the place of recompense and reckoning, for there is no benefit in that. I had already sent forth to you in the world the warning for whoever disbelieves in Me and disobeys Me."

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 50, verse 29:

"My word is not changed in My presence, and I do not wrong the servants by punishing one for another's sin. So I do not punish anyone except for his own sin, after the proof has been established against him."

Mention, O Messenger, to your people the Day when We say to Hell (Jahannam) on the Day of Resurrection: "Are you filled?" And Hell says: "Is there any more?" from among the jinn and mankind. Then the Lord, Majestic is His majesty, places His foot in it, so that parts of it draw together, one within another, and it says: "Qatt, qatt" (enough, enough), meaning: "I have had enough; I am full, and there is no room left in me."
The Paradise is brought near to the God-fearing, a place not far from them, so they behold it as an increase in their joy.

It is said to them: "This is what you were promised, O God-fearing ones, for every penitent returning from his sins, and a keeper of all that brought him near to his Lord, of the obligations and acts of obedience; for he who feared Allah in this world and meets Him on the Day of Resurrection with a heart penitent from its sins."

It is said to them: "This is what you were promised, O God-fearing ones, for every penitent returning from his sins, and a keeper of all that brought him near to his Lord, of the obligations and acts of obedience; for he who feared Allah in this world and meets Him on the Day of Resurrection with a heart penitent from its sins."
It shall be said to these believers: "Enter Paradise in safety, free from every calamity and evil, with every hateful thing kept far from you. That is the Day of Eternity, which never ends."
For these believers there is in Paradise whatever they desire. And with Us is an increase of bliss beyond what We have given them, the greatest of which is beholding the Noble Face of Allah.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 50, verse 36:

And We destroyed before these disbelievers of Quraysh many nations that were stronger than them in might and power. They roamed through the lands and traversed every path, seeking a way to escape destruction. Was there any escape from the punishment of Allah when it came upon them?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 50, verse 37:

Indeed, in the destruction of the past generations there is a lesson for whoever has a heart with which he understands, or who gives ear while being present in heart, neither heedless nor inattentive.

And We certainly created the seven heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, of various kinds of creatures, in six days, and no weariness touched Us from that creation. In this great power there is proof of His power—glory be to Him—to bring the dead back to life, all the more so.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 50, verses 39–40:

So be patient, O Messenger, over what the deniers say. Indeed, Allah is ever watchful over them. And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and pray in the night too, and glorify your Lord with His praise after the prayers.

Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death in this world, and to Us all of them will return on the Day of Resurrection, for reckoning and recompense. On the Day when the earth splits open, releasing the dead who are buried in it, they will come out hastening toward the Caller. That gathering before the Reckoning is easy and effortless for Us.

We know best what these polytheists say of falsehood against Allah and denial of His signs. You, O Messenger, are not a compeller over them, to force them into Islam. You were only sent as a conveyer of the message. So remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My threat, for whoever does not fear the threat will not be reminded.
